findings.description: The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. User data can be retrieved by principals or workloads with instance/metadata access, exposing the database credential.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it public network reachability. Although the shown security-group ingress is limited to the VPC CIDR, this unnecessarily exposes the database to internet-facing network paths and increases attack surface.
The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage and related snapshots unencrypted at rest.

The EC2 application role is granted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Compromise of the application instance or its role credentials would enable broad control and data access across these AWS services.
